claims.proposition: The 2017 residential-rental amendment sets out enumerated grounds and bounded amounts for realization of tenant security.
claims.does_not_support: Whether a particular tenancy meets applicability rules, whether unchanged 2026 law controls, or whether an individual cheque can be paid by a bank.

claims.proposition: The enacted 2017 wording requires reasonable advance notice before realization and reasonable opportunity to remedy.
claims.does_not_support: A universal fixed 7-day or 14-day period; legal correctness of any synthetic contract notice period.

claims.proposition: The enacted 2017 wording specifies a security-return mechanism tied to apartment return or clearing covered tenant debts.
claims.does_not_support: That different instruments in synthetic cases have identical contractual return dates or that the provision governs every agreement.

claims.proposition: The 2017 amount-cap wording concerns security involving tenant financial outlay; applicability exclusions are separately specified.
claims.does_not_support: A mechanical three-month cap on every security cheque or a verified statement of present-day applicability.

claims.proposition: The January 2026 government proposal discusses adding non-bank guarantee providers to the statutory definition.
claims.does_not_support: That the proposal text was enacted verbatim, that it is effective on 2026-09-22, or that any specific supplier qualifies.

claims.proposition: The enacted amendment replaces §25י(a) with definitions including other licensed guarantee providers and amends the opening of §25י(b) to include guarantees from those providers alongside bank guarantees.
claims.does_not_support: Which statutory version governs a particular lease, whether a particular provider is licensed, or whether a security cheque or note is subject to the financial-outlay cap.

claims.proposition: The official procedure index excerpt distinguishes merely holding a security check from circumstances after bank presentation and dishonor when opening an execution file.
claims.does_not_support: That the wording on a cheque prevents bank presentation, or that execution is lawful in a particular rental dispute.

claims.proposition: The authority publishes an execution-file opening route for unpaid checks and promissory notes.
claims.does_not_support: That the two instruments merge, share an amount, or are collectible in any particular case.

claims.proposition: The authority publishes an opposition route for debtors facing check/promissory-note execution for all or part of the claim.
claims.does_not_support: Whether an objection succeeds, whether a claim is valid, or a filing deadline absent verified rules.
